title: Quality of Earnings Preparation
summary: Preparing a portfolio company for buyer-grade EBITDA scrutiny before launching an exit process.
definition: Quality of Earnings Preparation is the seller-side process of cleaning financials, defending adjusted EBITDA, proving revenue quality, and eliminating diligence friction before a sale.
whyItMatters: PE cares because weak QofE support invites retrades, compresses the multiple, and converts value creation claims into buyer skepticism.
commonProblems: Adjusted EBITDA includes fragile or poorly documented add-backs.
Revenue, margin, and working capital data do not reconcile cleanly.
Management cannot explain variance without relying on anecdotes.
diagnosticQuestions: Which EBITDA adjustments would survive hostile buyer diligence?
Where do revenue quality, margin, or customer concentration issues weaken the exit story?
What must be cleaned before vendor diligence begins?
dataNeeded: Monthly P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow detail
Trial balance, general ledger, and chart of accounts
Customer revenue, churn, cohort, contract, and margin data
Working capital schedules and historical peg support
process: Build the normalized EBITDA bridge and classify every add-back by defensibility.
Reconcile revenue, margin, and working capital data across finance systems.
Identify buyer objection areas and assign remediation owners.
Prepare management explanations for variance, revenue quality, and margin movement.
Run a mock diligence review before commissioning vendor QofE.
ebitdaLogic: Clean earnings support protects the EBITDA base buyers multiply at exit and reduces the probability that diligence converts operating noise into purchase price reductions.
caseExample: A sponsor-backed services company removes weak add-backs, rebuilds customer-level margin support, reconciles deferred revenue, and enters sale diligence with a buyer-ready EBITDA bridge.
hundredDayPlan: Days 1-30: collect financial data, identify add-backs, map reconciliation gaps.
Days 31-60: rebuild EBITDA bridge, clean revenue and working capital support, draft variance explanations.
Days 61-100: run mock QofE, close data gaps, prepare vendor diligence package.
commonMistakes: Waiting until the sale process to discover broken financial support.
Treating every management adjustment as buyer-acceptable EBITDA.
Ignoring revenue quality while obsessing over accounting cleanup.

articleSections.title: Diagnose Readiness Before the Sale Clock Starts
body: Begin six to nine months before launch with a readiness diagnostic that treats the buyer's likely procedures as the standard. The CFO and controller should tie twenty-four to thirty-six months of monthly trial balances to audited statements, tax returns, bank activity, and management reporting; inventory every manual journal, revenue-recognition judgment, related-party item, and chart-of-accounts change; and document who can reproduce each schedule. The sponsor operating partner owns the readiness gate, but finance owns the numbers. A green rating requires source-level reconciliation, a named preparer and reviewer, and a repeatable monthly update—not merely a plausible explanation in a meeting.

Score risk across earnings, revenue, working capital, tax, systems, and management readiness. Quantify each issue by EBITDA, cash, or process impact and separate historical cleanup from forward operating improvement. A late close, inconsistent customer IDs, or unsupported backlog may not immediately change reported profit, yet each increases buyer effort and the discount applied to uncertainty. Hold a weekly readiness meeting during diagnosis, then move to biweekly remediation. Items remain open until evidence is stored in the indexed data room and independently reperformed; verbal assurance never changes a red item to green.

Set launch gates early: monthly statements closed within eight business days for three consecutive periods; trial balance and key subledgers reconciled; customer revenue and gross profit tied to the ledger; add-backs supported by invoices, payroll, contracts, or board records; and net working capital reproduced using the contemplated purchase-agreement definition. If the company cannot meet these tests, delay vendor diligence or narrow the claim. Starting a process with unresolved foundational gaps forces bankers to sell around facts, consumes management during bidder access, and gives buyers a reason to widen scope or reserve value.
articleSections.callout: Readiness is achieved when a skeptical third party can reproduce the answer from source evidence without management narration.

articleSections.title: Build the Reported-to-Adjusted EBITDA Schedule
body: Construct one monthly bridge from audited or reviewed operating income through reported EBITDA, management adjustments, run-rate items, and the proposed sell-side adjusted EBITDA. Every line needs a definition, period, accounting location, cash effect, tax effect, source file, owner, and status under the likely buyer standard. Classify adjustments as transaction-related, owner-specific, discontinued, nonrecurring, accounting normalization, or prospective synergy. Do not net favorable and unfavorable items or bury recurring misses inside a broad restructuring label. The schedule should expose judgment so management can remove weak claims before credibility is spent defending them.

Consider a company with $18.0 million of reported EBITDA. Management proposes $1.4 million of transaction fees, $0.9 million of owner costs, $1.2 million of restructuring, and $1.5 million of annualized savings, producing $23.0 million. Review shows that $0.3 million of transaction fees belongs to an ordinary refinancing, $0.4 million of restructuring recurs annually, and only $0.9 million of savings is implemented and visible in payroll or supplier invoices. The defensible bridge is $18.0 + $1.1 + $0.9 + $0.8 + $0.9 = $21.7 million. At an 11x multiple, removing $1.3 million of fragile adjustments prevents a potential $14.3 million credibility-driven retrade rather than sacrificing value.

The controller refreshes the bridge at every close; functional owners certify operational evidence; the CFO approves accounting treatment; and the sponsor and sell-side adviser challenge materiality monthly. Prospective items should show implementation date, one-time cost, realized-to-date benefit, remaining run rate, and whether market convention is likely to accept them. Freeze definitions ninety days before launch unless new facts require change. Version control and a decision log matter because a number that shifts between the confidential information memorandum, management presentation, vendor report, and buyer model will be interpreted as control failure.

articleSections.title: Prove Revenue Quality, Working Capital, and the Data Room
body: Rebuild revenue from invoice or contract detail to the general ledger and then to the management cohort views used in the sale story. Reconcile bookings, billings, recognized revenue, deferred revenue, churn, expansion, backlog, and gross margin using stable customer and product identifiers. Test cut-off around quarter ends, credits issued after period close, pass-through revenue, rebates, implementation fees, and gross-versus-net presentation. If recurring revenue is claimed, define recurrence contractually and show retention on a consistent population; do not allow CRM labels to override invoice history or contract terms.

Prepare monthly net working capital by purchase-agreement account, not by a convenient management subtotal. Reconcile AR aging, inventory reserves, deferred revenue, accrued expenses, payables, and excluded debt-like items to the trial balance. Use at least twenty-four months to show seasonality and calculate the peg under trailing average, selected-month, and normalized operating cases. A $40 million revenue business with monthly NWC ranging from $5.2 million to $8.1 million can lose several million dollars at close if a seasonal trough is presented as normal. Explain anomalies before negotiations and keep cash, debt, debt-like, and working-capital classifications mutually exclusive.

Design the data room as an evidence system. Each request maps to an authoritative file, preparation date, owner, reviewer, ledger tie-out, and approved external version. Finance should run a weekly completeness report and prohibit duplicate schedules with competing definitions. Access controls must protect employee, customer, and pricing data while leaving a clear audit trail. A response service-level of two business days is useful only if answers are reconciled; speed without quality creates follow-up questions. The goal is for the vendor provider, bankers, and management to draw from one controlled source rather than three privately maintained models.

articleSections.title: Run Mock Diligence and Close the Remediation Loop
body: At roughly ninety days before launch, assign an independent internal team or adviser to behave like a skeptical buy-side provider. Give them the EBITDA bridge, customer cube, revenue-recognition policies, working-capital schedule, cash proof, and selected contracts without coaching. Require them to reproduce headline metrics and issue a request list. Conduct management sessions on unexplained monthly movements, customer concentration, margin durability, add-back eligibility, and cash conversion. Questions that require offline reconstruction expose a process gap even when the final answer proves correct.

Convert findings into a remediation register with monetary exposure, root cause, corrective action, owner, due date, evidence, and disclosure decision. The CFO chairs a weekly closure meeting; legal decides privilege and disclosure implications; the CEO resolves cross-functional delays; and the deal lead controls scope. A finding closes only after reperformance. Where history cannot be repaired—such as missing contract amendments or unreliable legacy SKU detail—quantify the limitation, build a conservative alternative analysis, and align the narrative. Concealment is worse than a bounded weakness because discovery late in exclusivity invites both price and trust penalties.

Use a twelve-week preparation sequence: weeks one through three diagnose and reconcile; weeks four through seven rebuild EBITDA, revenue, and NWC schedules; weeks eight and nine complete data-room indexing and management drafts; week ten runs mock diligence; weeks eleven and twelve remediate and retest. Escalate any unresolved issue above an agreed EBITDA or cash threshold to the board transaction committee. Do not compress by skipping independent challenge. If mock results reveal material revenue cut-off, an unreconciled ledger, or multiple unsupported adjustments, reset the launch date rather than hoping competitive tension will suppress technical diligence.

articleSections.title: Sustain Buyer-Grade Reporting and Validate Exit Proof
body: After vendor work begins, maintain a monthly roll-forward that bridges the original reference period to current trading. New months must use the same customer, EBITDA, and NWC definitions and separately show budget variance, acquisition impact, foreign exchange, price, volume, mix, and one-time items. The CFO certifies the update within ten business days; the deal team reconciles it to marketing materials; and the board reviews deviations that could trigger disclosure. Avoid improving a metric by changing cohorts or classifications. Buyers will compare every successive file and interpret unexplained favorable revisions as earnings management.

Validate value-creation benefits through a ledger that distinguishes gross action, leakage, one-time cost, realized P&L benefit, cash benefit, and approved add-back. For example, a procurement program targeting $2.0 million may show $1.6 million of invoice-rate reduction, $0.2 million of adverse mix, and $0.1 million of implementation cost, leaving $1.4 million of recurring EBITDA and $1.3 million first-year cash benefit. Tie results to invoices and purchase volumes, not forecasts. Maintain controls after the deal launches so accepted improvements do not reverse during diligence and undermine both the adjusted EBITDA bridge and the management forecast.

Exit proof is a reproducible package: three clean closes, an indexed bridge with support, customer and product data tied to revenue, a normalized NWC range, documented accounting policies, a closed remediation log, management-ready explanations, and a roll-forward with forecast accuracy. Buyer confidence is visible in fewer duplicate requests, limited diligence adjustments, stable financing cases, and no late surprise between signing and closing. Preserve these routines after a failed or delayed process; readiness should become the company's reporting standard, not a temporary deal-room performance that disappears when the transaction calendar changes.
